people.summary: Born 21 October 1872 and baptised at Ward End, Aston, on 19 June 1873, son of William and Fanny Mary Fitzmaurice. An engineer all his working life. He married Edith Madeline Spencer at St Matthew's, Brixton, on 2 August 1897. He lived in Cape Town from 1916 to about 1923. He died on 7 June 1928, probably aged 55, and was buried at Chingford Mount. He was not a son of the Earls of Orkney.
people.story:
Edward Dixon FitzMaurice was born on 21 October 1872 and baptised on 19 June 1873 at St Margaret's, Ward End, Aston. The register names his parents as William and Fanny Mary Fitzmaurice, of Ward End, and his father as a surveyor and contractor.[^parish-wardend-1873] His own marriage register names that father as Robert William Fitzmaurice, a contractor.[^parish-brixton-1897] The birth index gives his mother's maiden name as Falcke.[^gro-indexes] In 1881 he is the boy written as Ernest Dixon, aged 8, born at Little Bromwich, in the household of Robert William FitzMaurice and Fanny Mary at Aston Manor.[^census-1881-aston]

In 1891 he was an apprentice civil engineer, a lodger at 25 Compton Avenue, Brighton, born at Ward End.[^census-1891-brighton] On 2 August 1897, aged 25 and a professional singer, he married Edith Madeline Spencer at St Matthew's, Brixton, by banns.[^parish-brixton-1897] He was probably a civil mechanical engineer in Brixton in 1901.[^census-1901-brixton] In 1911 he was a civil engineer at Whitstable, with Edith and three children.[^census-1911-whitstable]

In the middle of the First World War, by then a civil engineer of about 43, he sailed from London for South Africa on the Balmoral Castle on 29 March 1916, meaning to settle there.[^passenger-1916-balmoral] Five months later Edith probably followed on the Llanstephan Castle with Bob, Reg and Eileen.[^passenger-1916-llanstephan] He came back to England in October 1923, giving Whitstable as his address, and sailed for Cape Town again that December.[^passenger-1923-armadale] [^passenger-1923-arundel] Edith came home in November 1925.[^passenger-1925-edith]

He died on 7 June 1928, probably aged 55, and was buried at Chingford Mount Cemetery.[^findagrave-214209661] [^burial-chingford-1928] When Eileen married in 1936, the paper remembered him as formerly of Cape Town.[^news-1936-simmons]

Edward was an engineer all his working life: an apprentice civil engineer in 1891, a civil engineer in 1901 and 1911, and an engineer on every passenger list from 1916 to 1923. The white collar in the beach photo is not a sign that he was a clergyman.[^beach-snapshots]

He was not a son of the Hon. Henry Warrender FitzMaurice. The London Gazette of 23 April 1890 names the 7th Earl of Orkney's surviving brother and sister, and Edward is not among them.[^gazette-1890]

people.summary: Reg's mother, not his sister. Edith Madeline Spencer married Edward Dixon FitzMaurice on 2 August 1897. She was probably born about 1866 to 1869 in Islington. She probably died in the Bridge district of Kent in early 1929, aged 61. She was probably in South Africa from about 1916 to 1925.
people.story:
The medallion portrait inscribed Edith Madeleine Fitzmaurice, about 1899, is Edith Madeline Spencer, Edward Dixon's wife and Reg's mother. Earlier pages that called her Reg's sister were wrong.[^edith-medallion] [^parish-brixton-1897]

She was probably born about 1866 to 1869 in Islington. In 1891 she was 22, a governess, born in Islington, living with her widowed mother Caroline at 15 Mornington Place, St Pancras. The house number may read 15b.[^census-1891-spencer] Her death in 1929, aged 61, fits that birth. At the wedding she was recorded as 24, and in 1911 as 38 and born at St Anne, Soho. Those later ages are the odd ones out. Her birth registration has not been found. A birth of Edith Maria Spencer at Islington in 1866 belongs to a different family and is not hers.[^census-1891-spencer] [^gro-edith-death] [^census-1911-whitstable]

On 2 August 1897 she married Edward at St Matthew's, Brixton. Her father, Charles Spencer, a builder and contractor, was already dead. Caroline Spencer was a witness.[^parish-brixton-1897] In 1911, at Whitstable, she and Edward had had four children, of whom three were living. The child who had died was Edith Marjorie.[^census-1911-whitstable] She probably died in the March quarter of 1929 in the Bridge district of Kent, aged 61.[^gro-edith-death]

She probably went out to Cape Town in August 1916 with Bob, Reg and Eileen. At the end of 1923 she came to London with Reg and Eileen on the Bendigo, landing on 28 December 1923, and gave 140A Clapham Road, London S.W. (the number is hard to read).[^passenger-1923-bendigo] She came back to England from South Africa in November 1925, aged 53 by her own account, giving Birkenhead as her destination.[^passenger-1916-llanstephan] [^passenger-1925-edith]

people.story:
Reg was Baron Reginald FitzMaurice. Baron is a forename, not a title. He was probably born on 26 May 1904 in the Wandsworth district. The birth index names his mother as Spenser, a spelling of Spencer, volume 1d, page 670.[^gro-indexes] [^probate-reg-1977] In 1911 he is Baron Reginald, aged 6, at school, in Edward Dixon and Edith Madeline's household at Whitstable.[^census-1911-whitstable]

He probably married Lilian Maud Mary Bennett in the December quarter of 1927, in the Hammersmith district, volume 1a, page 661.[^gro-marriage-1927] Electoral registers place him in Wandsworth in 1925 and 1926, Hammersmith from 1931 to 1933, the Spelthorne district from 1934 to 1937, and Hayes from 1938 until about 1972.[^electoral-fitzmaurice] On 11 February 1950 he gave his daughter Patricia away at St Mary's, Wanstead. The album calls him Mr R. Fitzmaurice of Hayes.[^album-1950]

He died on 31 March 1977. The death was registered at Hillingdon, and the probate calendar places him at Hayes. The estate was 24,427 pounds.[^probate-reg-1977] A cause of death remembered in the family is not on the certificate we have, so it is not stated here. A studio portrait of a young man in a bow tie has no name on it, and it is not identified as Reg.

He was probably the boy of 12 on the same voyage to Cape Town in August 1916.[^passenger-1916-llanstephan] He came back to London with his mother and Eileen on the Bendigo, landing on 28 December 1923, listed as Baron Fitzmaurice, a student, aged 19.[^passenger-1923-bendigo]

people.story:
The wedding album's late Mrs R. Fitzmaurice was probably Lilian Maud Mary Bennett. She was born about March 1900 at Bodmin, Cornwall. The birth index, June quarter 1900, volume 5c, page 64, names her mother as Grigg, and the 1921 census gives the same three forenames, aged 21 years and 3 months, born at Bodmin.[^gro-lilian-death] [^census-1921-lilian] [^census-bennett]

Her parents were Charles Bennett, a tailor of Egloshayle and Bodmin, and Annie, probably Matilda Ann Nicholls Grigg. Lilian was the youngest of the children who survived. In June 1921 she was a clerk at the Claims Record Office, boarding at Hampton Hill.[^census-1921-lilian] She probably married Baron Reginald FitzMaurice in the December quarter of 1927, in the Hammersmith district.[^gro-marriage-1927]

She probably died in the December quarter of 1947, in the Uxbridge district, which covered Hayes, aged 47.[^gro-lilian-death] The album of February 1950 therefore calls her the late Mrs R. Fitzmaurice.[^album-1950] No will and no grave have been found. A family memory that she died while Pat was a young child does not fit an age of about 18.

people.summary: Reg's brother, called Bob. Edward Robert FitzMaurice, born in the Lambeth district in 1901. He married in Cape Town in 1925 and died at Port Elizabeth on 7 May 1981.
people.story:
The beach photograph is labelled Reg, Bob and their father Edward Dixon Fitzmaurice. Bob is Edward Robert Fitzmaurice, mother's maiden name Spencer, registered in the Lambeth district in the June quarter of 1901, volume 1d, page 503. In 1911 he was 9, at school, at Whitstable. He was probably the boy of 15 who sailed to Cape Town with his mother in August 1916.

On 30 October 1925, aged 24, a tramway engineer, he married Eileen Alice Yallop at St George's Cathedral, Cape Town. He was living at Auleta, Three Anchor Bay, and she at 7 Bertram Road, Sea Point. In 1926 their home was 17 Berkley Street, Gardens, when their son Edward Scott was baptised in the parish of Woodstock. Edward Scott died on 9 August 1935, aged 9, at Somerset Hospital. The home was then given as 1st Avenue, Bellville. Edward Robert died on 7 May 1981 at Port Elizabeth.

people.summary: Ron's father. Henry George Andrews, born at St Albans in April 1889, only child of Herbert Andrews and Lucy Stacey. He married Rosina Maud Cousins on 18 April 1915. He, Rosina and their son Sidney were killed at their home in Plaistow on 19 April 1941.
people.story:
Henry George Andrews was born at St Albans, Hertfordshire, in April 1889, and baptised at St Albans Abbey on 9 June 1889, son of Herbert and Lucy.[^parish-st-albans-1889] The birth index names his mother as Stacey.[^gro-indexes] He was their only child.[^census-andrews-stacey] In 1901 the family was at Hemel Hempstead. In 1911 he was a sawyer's labourer, living with his parents at Canning Town.

On 18 April 1915, aged 25, he married Rosina Maud Cousins at St Andrew's, Plaistow. His father is Herbert Andrews. Hers is William Cousins.[^parish-plaistow-1915] In 1921 he was a dock labourer for the Port of London Authority at the Royal Albert Docks, living at Plaistow in his father-in-law's house. In 1939 he was an explosive worker at the Royal filling factory, Woolwich.[^census-cousins] [^register-1939]

He was killed on 19 April 1941, aged 52, at the family home in Plaistow, in the West Ham county borough, together with Rosina and their son Sidney.[^cwgc-plaistow-1941] The wedding album's East Ham is the neighbouring borough. The Commonwealth War Graves record gives Plaistow.

people.story:
Rosina Maud Cousins was born on 14 November 1881 at Bermondsey, and registered in the St Olave district, volume 1d, page 292. Her mother's maiden name was Gall.[^gro-cousins-gall] She was one of eight children of William Cousins, a dock labourer born at Hackney, and Annie, nee Gall, born at Thetford.[^census-cousins]

On 18 April 1915 she married Henry George Andrews at St Andrew's, Plaistow.[^parish-plaistow-1915] Their children were Herbert William, Ronald and Sidney George. The home in Plaistow had been her father's. She, Henry and Sidney were killed there on 19 April 1941. Rosina was 59.[^cwgc-plaistow-1941]

people.summary: King of Scots from the age of six, after the murder of his father in 1437. He was killed when one of his own cannon exploded at the siege of Roxburgh in 1460.
people.story:
James II became King of Scots in 1437, at the age of six, after his father James I was murdered. He was known as "Fiery Face" for a red birthmark on one side of his face.[^wiki-james-ii]

He married Mary of Guelders in 1449. In August 1460 he was besieging Roxburgh Castle, then held by the English, when one of his cannon exploded beside him and killed him. He was 29.[^wiki-james-ii]

His daughter Mary Stewart married into the Hamilton family, and through her the Hamiltons came close to the Scottish throne.[^wiki-mary-stewart]

people.story:
Mary Stewart was the elder daughter of King James II and Mary of Guelders. By 1467 she had been married to Thomas Boyd, who was made Earl of Arran. His family fell from power and the marriage was annulled.[^wiki-mary-stewart]

In 1474 she married James, 1st Lord Hamilton, who was almost forty years older than her. A papal dispensation for the marriage followed in 1476.[^wiki-mary-stewart] Their son James became the 1st Earl of Arran.[^wiki-arran-1][^aah-hamilton] Earlier pages called that son her grandson, which is wrong, and gave her dates as about 1433 to 1465, which are also wrong.[^site-earlier]

No portrait of her is known. The portrait shown with her father is of her mother, Mary of Guelders.[^site-earlier]

people.story:
James Hamilton was the son of Mary Stewart and James, 1st Lord Hamilton, and so a grandson of King James II. He was made Earl of Arran.[^wiki-arran-1][^aah-hamilton]

He married first Elizabeth Home, in about 1490, and then Janet Bethune in 1516. His son by Janet became the 2nd Earl of Arran and Duke of Châtellerault.[^wiki-arran-1][^wiki-chatellerault]

Earlier pages called him Mary's grandson and said he was Regent of Scotland. He was her son, and it was his son, not he, who became Regent.[^site-earlier][^wiki-chatellerault]

people.story:
Lord George Hamilton was a son of Anne, Duchess of Hamilton, and William Douglas, and was baptised in February 1666.[^wiki-george-orkney] He was a soldier for most of his life and served under the Duke of Marlborough; earlier pages show him with the Battle of Blenheim of 1704.[^wiki-george-orkney][^site-earlier]

On 25 November 1695 he married Elizabeth Villiers, and on 3 January 1696 he was made Earl of Orkney.[^wiki-george-orkney] He bought Cliveden in Buckinghamshire and lived there and at Taplow.[^wiki-george-orkney] He was appointed Governor of Virginia but never went there. In 1736 he became the first officer in the British Army to hold the rank of Field Marshal, and he died in January 1737.[^wiki-george-orkney]

He had daughters but no son. The earldom could pass to a daughter, and his eldest, Anne, became the 2nd Countess.[^wiki-george-orkney][^wiki-anne-countess]

people.summary: Son of Henry Warrender. He succeeded his uncle as Earl in 1889, aged 22, and in 1892 married the Gaiety star Connie Gilchrist. Their only child died before him, and the title passed to a distant cousin.
people.story:
Edmond Walter FitzMaurice was the son of Henry Warrender FitzMaurice and Sarah Jane Roose. He succeeded his uncle George as 7th Earl of Orkney in October 1889, aged 22.[^peerage-henry-warrender][^wiki-6th-earl] In April 1890 a royal warrant gave his surviving brother and sister the rank of an earl's children; it names no other siblings.[^gazette-1890]

On 19 July 1892 he married Connie Gilchrist, a former child performer of the Gaiety Theatre.[^wiki-connie] The Evening News of 1951 describes him as of The Tythe House, Stewkley, near Leighton Buzzard, a Deputy Lieutenant for Buckinghamshire and a former Master of the Whaddon Chase Foxhounds.[^korea-clipping]

Their only child, Lady Mary Constance Hamilton FitzMaurice, was born in 1903. She married, had no children, and died in October 1950, ten months before her father.[^peerage-henry-warrender][^wiki-connie] When Edmond died in August 1951 he left the residue of his estate of £42,893 to Cecil FitzMaurice, who also inherited the earldom. The paper called Edmond Cecil's great-uncle; by the peerage records he was Cecil's first cousin twice removed.[^korea-clipping][^press-1951][^peerage-cecil]

Earlier pages give his name as "Edmond Walter Leighton FitzMaurice" and say he inherited at 16. "Leighton" comes from the Leighton Buzzard address, and he was 22.[^site-earlier][^korea-clipping]

EARL FROM KOREA LEFT A FORTUNE
HE SCRUBBED DECKS
[handwritten: 1951]
"Evening News" Reporter
THIRTY-TWO-YEAR-OLD Cecil O'Bryen Fitzmaurice, who became the Eighth Earl of Orkney while serving as an R.A.S.C. driver in Korea, has been left the residue of a £42,893 estate by his great-uncle, the Seventh Earl, it is revealed to-day.
The Rt. Hon. Edmond Walter Fitzmaurice, Seventh Earl of Orkney, of The Tythe House, Stewkley, Leighton Buzzard, a Deputy Lieutenant for Buckinghamshire and a former Master of the Whaddon Chase Foxhounds, died last August, aged 84.

Late Back Aboard
The seventh Earl was married for 54 years to Miss Connie Gilchrist, the Gaiety star of the 'nineties who died in 1946, aged 73.
The new Earl, known to his friends as "Ginger" in the Army, arrived home by troopship last October.
On the way home the ship called at Colombo. For arriving back late he received four days C.B. and scrubbed mess-decks.
He is now living with his mother, Mrs. Dorothy Wiggins, at Lantern Hatch, Itchingfield, near Horsham, Sussex.

people.story:
Connie Gilchrist was born in January 1865. As a child she modelled for painters: Whistler painted her as "The Gold Girl", posed as she appeared on the Gaiety Theatre stage in her skipping-rope dance, and she was the girl in Frederic Leighton's "The Music Lesson".[^wiki-connie][^met-gold-girl] She performed at the Gaiety and became known as "the original Gaiety Girl".[^wiki-connie]

She had left the stage by July 1892, when she married Edmond FitzMaurice, 7th Earl of Orkney.[^wiki-connie] They were married for 54 years. She died in May 1946.[^wiki-connie][^korea-clipping] The 1951 newspaper report gives her age at death as 73; from her date of birth she was 81.[^korea-clipping][^wiki-connie]

people.summary: A distant cousin of the 7th Earl, he inherited the earldom in 1951 while serving as an Army driver in Korea. He married Rose Silley at Brixham in 1953.
people.story:
Cecil O'Bryen FitzMaurice was the younger son of Douglas Frederick Harold FitzMaurice and Dorothy Dickie. He joined the Royal Army Service Corps in 1939 and served in North Africa, Italy, France and Germany, and then in Korea.[^wiki-cecil][^peerage-cecil]

He became the 8th Earl of Orkney on 21 August 1951 while serving as a driver in Korea. Newspapers called him "the Earl from Korea".[^press-1951][^korea-clipping] The Evening News reported that his Army friends knew him as "Ginger", that the 7th Earl had left him the residue of an estate of £42,893, and that on the voyage home he was given four days' confinement to barracks and set to scrub the mess decks for coming back late to the ship at Colombo.[^korea-clipping] The paper called the 7th Earl his great-uncle; he was in fact a much more distant cousin.[^korea-clipping][^peerage-cecil]

On 27 November 1953 he married Rose Katherine Durk Silley at St Mary's, Brixham. The Evening News said she helped her mother run a 60-bedroom hotel in the town, and that the Earl had once worked in a garage.[^marries-clipping][^peerage-cecil] Rose died in 1995. Cecil died in February 1998 with no children, and the earldom passed to a distant cousin, Peter St John.[^wiki-cecil][^wiki-earl-of-orkney]

Earlier pages give the year of his marriage as 1952. The peerage records give 1953.[^site-earlier][^peerage-cecil]

EARL FROM KOREA LEFT A FORTUNE
HE SCRUBBED DECKS
[handwritten: 1951]
"Evening News" Reporter
THIRTY-TWO-YEAR-OLD Cecil O'Bryen Fitzmaurice, who became the Eighth Earl of Orkney while serving as an R.A.S.C. driver in Korea, has been left the residue of a £42,893 estate by his great-uncle, the Seventh Earl, it is revealed to-day.
The Rt. Hon. Edmond Walter Fitzmaurice, Seventh Earl of Orkney, of The Tythe House, Stewkley, Leighton Buzzard, a Deputy Lieutenant for Buckinghamshire and a former Master of the Whaddon Chase Foxhounds, died last August, aged 84.

Late Back Aboard
The seventh Earl was married for 54 years to Miss Connie Gilchrist, the Gaiety star of the 'nineties who died in 1946, aged 73.
The new Earl, known to his friends as "Ginger" in the Army, arrived home by troopship last October.
On the way home the ship called at Colombo. For arriving back late he received four days C.B. and scrubbed mess-decks.
He is now living with his mother, Mrs. Dorothy Wiggins, at Lantern Hatch, Itchingfield, near Horsham, Sussex.

people.summary: Clerk in the Board of Ordnance at the Tower of London. He married Eliza Taylor at St Martin's, Birmingham, on 3 February 1827. Father of William, John Richard and Robert William. By 1861 he was described as a gentleman. His birth, parents and death have not been found.
people.story: John FitzMaurice married Eliza Taylor by licence at St Martin's, Birmingham, on 3 February 1827. The register describes him as of His Majesty's Tower of London, a bachelor, and Eliza as of that parish, a spinster. John Taylor witnessed the marriage.[^parish-birmingham-1827] He was a clerk with the Board of Ordnance: a clerk at their son William's baptism in 1827, a clerk in the Ordnance Office in 1829, and a clerk in the Tower in 1832.[^parish-whitechapel-1827] [^parish-stepney-1829] [^parish-stepney-1832] The family lived in Whitechapel and then in Mile End Old Town. By 1861, when Robert William married, the register calls John a gentleman.[^parish-battersea-1861] His own birth, his parents and his death have not been found. A published family history places him in a Carlow branch of the FitzMaurices of Kerry. The London entries in that account now agree with these registers. No record found so far states where he was born or who his parents were, so that origin stays likely but not proved.[^fitzmaurice-family-carlow]

people.story:
Robert William FitzMaurice was baptised on 30 September 1832 at St Dunstan's, Stepney, son of John, a clerk in the Tower, and Eliza. The date usually given as his birth is this baptism. He was the youngest of three sons. William was born in 1827 and John Richard was baptised in 1829.[^parish-stepney-1832] [^parish-whitechapel-1827] [^parish-stepney-1829] On 14 September 1861, a surveyor, he married Fanny Mary Falcke at St Mary's, Battersea. His father John is called a gentleman on that register.[^parish-battersea-1861]

In 1871 he was a surveyor and contractor at Little Bromwich, Aston, born in Stepney.[^census-1871-aston] In 1881 he was a granite merchant and contractor at Aston Manor.[^census-1881-aston] He died at Edgbaston on 10 May 1895, aged 64. His estate was 12,921 pounds 4 shillings and 9 pence. The executors were his widow Fanny Mary and their sons John Rupert, a quarry owner, and Walter, a contractor.[^probate-robert-1895] When his son Edward married in 1897, the register names Robert William Fitzmaurice, contractor, as the father, and says he was already dead.[^parish-brixton-1897]

The baptism, the 1851 census and the 1881 census all give Battersea.[^census-1871-aston] [^census-1881-aston] She died at Erdington on 25 October 1917, aged 80.[^probate-fanny-1917] She was probably the mother of Edward Dixon: his birth index names the mother's maiden name as Falcke, and she was Robert William's wife.[^gro-indexes]

people.summary: Reg's younger sister, called Auntie Babs (confirmed by the family). Born late 1907 in the Blean district of Kent, daughter of Edward Dixon and Edith Madeline. She probably sailed to Cape Town in 1916, married Leslie Hugh Simmons at Staines in the summer of 1936, and probably died at Canterbury in early 1996.
people.story:
The youngest of Edward Dixon and Edith's children, Eileen was 3 at Whitstable in 1911.[^census-1911-whitstable] She was probably the girl of 8 who sailed to Cape Town with her mother and brothers in August 1916.[^passenger-1916-llanstephan] She came back to London from South Africa with her mother and Reg on the Bendigo, landing on 28 December 1923, aged 16.[^passenger-1923-bendigo] A snapshot of a girl on a verandah is labelled on the back Auntie Babs, South Africa, and the letters Eil are scratched into the front. The family confirms she was that girl.[^photo-labels] [^beach-snapshots]

She married Leslie Hugh Simmons, secretary of the Corinth Hockey Club, at Staines in the summer of 1936. The local paper called her the daughter of the late Mr Edward Dixon Fitzmaurice, formerly of Cape Town.[^news-1936-simmons] In 1939 the couple lived at Hayes, close to her brother Reg. Leslie was a rate fixer and motion study engineer.[^register-1939] As Auntie Babs she was at Pat's wedding in 1950, with Uncle Leslie beside her.[^album-1950]

In 1984 she married Ralph Hallawell in Kent, and she probably died at Canterbury in early 1996, aged 88.[^gro-indexes]

people.summary: Lilian's father. A tailor, later a general labourer, then a tailor and outfitter, born at Egloshayle in Cornwall about 1850. He and Annie were living apart in 1911. He probably died at Bodmin on 5 December 1925, aged 77.
people.story:
Charles Bennett was born at Egloshayle, Cornwall, about 1849 to 1851. In 1891 he was a tailor in Bodmin. In 1901 he was a general labourer at 1 Honey Street, Bodmin. In 1911 he was 62, a tailor and outfitter, born at Slades, Egloshayle, and living in Bodmin with his son Frank.[^census-bennett] He and Annie had probably married in 1882, in the Stoke Damerel district.[^gro-bennett-grigg]

In 1911 they were living apart in the same town. Annie, who kept a draper's shop, described herself as a widow, but Charles was alive. Both of their census forms say 11 children had been born, 8 were living and 3 had died.[^census-bennett] He probably died at Bodmin on 5 December 1925, aged 77. Administration of his estate, 296 pounds 1 shilling and 4 pence, was granted to May Bennett, a spinster. That grant does not, by itself, show which daughter she was.[^probate-charles-bennett-1926]

people.story:
William Cousins was probably baptised on 1 December 1850 at St John, Hackney, the son of William Cousins, a porter, and his wife Elizabeth.[^parish-hackney-1850] In 1861 the family was probably living at Mile End Old Town. His father was a messenger, and the children included a sister Amelia.[^census-1861-cousins]

On 15 January 1871, aged 21 and a clerk, he married Anne Gall at St Philip's, Stepney. The register names his father as William Cousins, a clerk.[^parish-stepney-1871] In 1881 he was a wharf foreman in Bermondsey. The later censuses take the family to West Ham. By 1901 Annie had died, and he was in Canning Town with Amelia and Herbert. In 1911 and 1921 he was at Plaistow, in 1921 a retired dock labourer in the household of his daughter Rosina and her husband Henry George.[^census-cousins]

He is named as Rosina's father on her marriage in 1915.[^parish-plaistow-1915] He probably died in the December quarter of 1922 in the West Ham district, volume 4a, page 53, aged 71.[^gro-cousins-gall]

people.summary: Auntie May. Rosina's younger sister, born in the spring of 1886 in the West Ham district. She never married. She lived at Chiswick, and died on 27 September 1971.
people.story:
May Florence Cousins, mother's maiden name Gall, was registered in the West Ham district in the June quarter of 1886, volume 4a, page 167.[^census-1921-may] She never married. In 1921 she was 35, a ward maid at East Ham Isolation Hospital. She later worked at Ealing, and in 1939 she was a dining hall maid at Colchester.[^census-1921-may] [^register-1939] From 1948 to 1967 the electoral registers place her at Chiswick and Gunnersbury, and then at Feltham.[^electoral-may] She died on 27 September 1971. The estate was 1,541 pounds.[^probate-may-1971]

This is the Auntie May Amanda remembered: an elderly aunt who had never married, who came to stay, and who lived at Chiswick. She was probably also the Auntie May named at Pat and Ron's wedding, though that last step is not proved. Lilian's sister Minnie is a different person.
